works.title: Why do i explain myself before I listen?
works.description: [Inferred] obedience
scripture: Why do I explain myself before I listen? Well
maybe because you don't actually want to hear what's being said. I mean
think about it. If your first response to correction is explaining or defending or debating
you can fill that entire conversation with reasons why the other person shouldn't believe what they're telling you. And sometimes that's the point. I mean
if you're busy building a defense
you don't have to seriously consider whether something might actually be wrong with you. But
accountability is one of the costs of real growth
and accountability becomes almost impossible when every criticism is immediately treated like an accusation that needs to be defeated. So
you can be incredibly skilled with words and still be terrible at listening. In fact
a way of dazzling people with explanations so nobody gets enough silence to examine the actual problem. And sometimes the most mature response to an accusation is simply
tell me more. And then stop talking. Hear them out. You can decide afterward whether they're right
because giving someone room to speak isn't an admission of guilt. And sometimes it's actually the clearest evidence of innocence
and a genuine desire for reconciliation. You don't have to defend yourself before you've even understood the charge.

works.title: Why should I read the Bible?

Hey everyone! Why is the Bible such a powerful book, you ask? Well, it's simple. The Bible is the inspired word of God, coming from a source beyond our understanding. Its timeless wisdom and unique insights speak to the very core of our existence. This ancient text reveals not just myths, but our real-life history and purpose. By exploring its pages, we gain profound answers to life's biggest questions - who we are, where we come from, and where we're headed.

But here's the thing, even from a non-religious perspective, the Bible remains the most influential book in shaping our world. Ignoring it means missing out on a key part of understanding our past, present, and future. Whether you're a believer or not, delving into its pages offers a deep connection to our roots and heritage. It's not about blind faith, it's about exploring profound truths that transcend human knowledge alone.

So, are you ready to discover what lies beyond the surface? Dive into the Bible and unlock a perspective that could change your life forever. #Bible #Inspiration #History #Culture

The text ultimately encourages individuals to consider whether their personal sense of good aligns with their moral compass, which is influenced by their understanding of God.

#bad #good #God #advice #Morality #Ethics #DeepThoughts

works.title: "I'm worried to do anything in life because what I do will have a bad consequence."
works.description:
The text reflects on the fear that many people have about the potential negative consequences of their actions. It emphasizes the importance of trust and faith, particularly for believers, suggesting that God always works things out for those who love Him. Even if the outcome isn’t what one expects, it is believed to be the best option in the end. The text also touches on the comfort found in the idea of being with God, even in death, and highlights the necessity of stepping forward in faith and relying on God’s promises, similar to facing everyday uncertainties.

#Faith #TrustInGod #BelieveInHisPlan

works.title: "It doesn't make you a bad follower of Christ if you are scared of death"
works.description:
The text emphasizes that feeling scared of death doesn’t make someone a bad follower of Christ. What matters is how one chooses to face death. The focus should be on having faith beyond feelings and recognizing the inevitability of death for everyone. It encourages considering Christ’s example of overcoming death and finding hope in his experience. While fear is understandable, the key is not to be overcome by it, but to find strength and hope in Christ’s approach to facing death.

#death #scared #biblical #advice #life #god #FaithOverFear #HopeInChrist #EmbracingLife

works.title: "I'm not going to come to church because when I was younger I had a bad experience."
works.description:
The speaker acknowledges that some individuals may have had negative experiences at church in the past, but emphasizes that the purpose of attending church is not solely for personal fulfillment. Instead, they argue that being part of a covenant community involves creating new, positive experiences and upholding accountability, counseling, and right doctrine within the community. They stress that avoiding church due to past negative experiences will not resolve the issue, and assert that being a complete Christian involves active involvement in a faith community, including regular attendance at church. Ultimately, the speaker suggests that this obligation should be taken up with God.

#goingtochurch #badexperience #church #advice #bible #FaithCommunity #PositiveExperiences #ChurchAttendance

works.title: "Can I rebuild my life on the foundation of my positive traits?"
works.description:
The text discusses the idea of rebuilding one’s life on positive traits and suggests that this is not a stable foundation, as people and their characters change over time. The author emphasizes the importance of relying on something transcendent and unchanging, such as God, as a stable foundation for life. They caution that building one’s life on something that changes leaves one vulnerable to significant distress when faced with stronger forces, such as traumatic events.

#goodfoundation #biblical #advice #change #positivity #StabilityInTranscendence #BuildingOnTheUnchanging #FindYourFoundation

works.title: "Why does God always have me doing things I don't want to do?"
works.description:
The text addresses the common question of why God often leads individuals to do things they don’t want to do. It encourages a shift in perspective, asking why people are drawn to actions contrary to what God desires. It emphasizes the importance of having an infinite mindset and trusting that God’s intentions, even when challenging, are ultimately for one’s benefit. The passage highlights that because God is good, His directives, though not always easy, are aimed at what is best for individuals. It draws parallels with everyday challenges like eating vegetables, exercising, or showing love in difficult situations. Ultimately, it advocates for considering what is truly beneficial and trusting in God’s goodness, rather than solely seeking what is comfortable or easy.

#life #advice #bible #whatisgoodforyou #TrustGod #InfiniteMindset #EmbraceChallenges

works.title: "Why do we need to give something back to God?"
works.description:
The text discusses the concept of giving back to God and the reasons behind it. It highlights the idea that giving to God is not about expecting something in return, like a genie granting wishes, but rather about expressing love and gratitude for what has been provided. The author emphasizes the importance of reciprocity and the desire to share with someone you love. It also references examples from scripture, such as Abraham’s voluntary tithe and instances in the New Testament where giving is emphasized as a way to express love and devotion to God. Ultimately, the central message is that giving to God is an act of love and a means of nurturing a deeper relationship with Him.

#givingtogod #give #love #advice #bible #GiveToGod #Spirituality #LoveAndGratitude

works.title: "Will I ever be able to go back to my addiction without it having control of my life?"
works.description:
The text discusses the process of recovering from addictions and behaviors that have taken control of one’s life. It emphasizes that the ability to engage with these things in a healthy manner is largely dependent on one’s relationship with God. While society often claims “once an addict, always an addict,” or “once a cheater, always a cheater,” the text suggests that God can transform lives and help individuals develop healthy relationships with previously harmful behaviors. It offers hope for those struggling with issues such as overeating, sex, anger, and language, emphasizing the possibility of transformation and change through a new connection with God.

#addiction #godsgrace #healing #advice #bible #Transformation #Hope #Faith #Recovery #NewBeginnings

works.title: "How do I correct someone who is making bad choices?"
works.description:
The text discusses the approach to correcting someone who is making unhealthy or unethical choices. It emphasizes the importance of addressing the issue truthfully and honestly rather than avoiding the truth. The text suggests that individuals making such choices may be seeking honesty and that addressing the problem directly is essential. Furthermore, it advocates for a mindset focused on reconciliation, aiming to bring the person back into correction rather than treating them as the problem. The ultimate goal is resolution, and the approach should be honest, gentle, and oriented towards reconciliation.

#biblicaltruth #biblicaladvice #counselling #advice #Honesty #Reconciliation #EthicalChoices #HealthyMindset

works.title: "How do I act when something bad is happening to somebody that is bad?"
works.description:
The text discusses how Christians should respond when bad things happen to bad people. It emphasizes that one’s response should be rooted in personal values rather than the actions of others. The author suggests that treating bad people with love and care, regardless of their behavior, reflects the humanitarian and godly love that should be extended to everyone. The text ultimately encourages responding to bad situations by showing the same love that God extends to all, irrespective of their actions.
 
#badthing #deserve #bad #good #godslove #advice #LoveInAction #CompassionateResponse #ReflectingGodsLove

works.title: "What do I do when, I feel like no one likes me?"
works.description:
When feeling unliked, it’s common to doubt oneself. The advice is to remember that one is unique and loved by God. Connecting with a community, whether it’s family, friends, or school, can provide support and perspective. Often, people may actually like you but may be hesitant to show it. Reconnecting with faith and seeking guidance from God can offer solace and strength during such times.

#biblicaltruth #biblicaladvice #FaithStrength #CommunitySupport

works.title: "Why do I always have to make all the decisions in my life?"
works.description:
The text explores the idea that having the freedom to make decisions, even difficult ones, is an essential part of being human. It emphasizes that our ability to make choices, both good and bad, is tied to our possession of free will and agency. The author suggests that if all decisions were made for us, we would lose the essence of what it means to be human. Despite the challenges that come with decision-making, the text ultimately portrays it as a necessary and valuable aspect of our existence.

#choices #freewill #bible #advice #FreeWill #HumanExperience #Empowerment

works.title: "I can't keep all my anger in, sometimes I have to let it out."
works.description:
The text discusses the concept of expressing anger and the need for control in doing so. It emphasizes that while it’s important to address anger, it should be done in a controlled manner without sinning. The author references the Bible to support the idea that it’s acceptable to feel anger, but it must be managed appropriately, considering love for others and adherence to God’s laws. Ultimately, the text asserts that individuals don’t have an unrestricted right to release their anger but rather need to exercise discretion and discernment.

#anger #justice #bible #advice #wise #AngerManagement #BiblicalWisdom #EmotionalIntelligence

works.title: "Why does God tempt me with bad things?"
works.description:
The text emphasizes that although God allows people to face temptations and unjust suffering in an imperfect world, it is incorrect to blame Him for leading individuals into wrongdoing. Instead, the text argues that when faced with opportunities to do wrong, there is always a way to choose the right path, as God desires. The presence of sin within humans is highlighted as the true cause of wrongdoing, rather than God’s influence. The text encourages individuals to focus on God and take responsibility for their actions rather than blaming Him for their choices.
 
#tempt #God #good #choices #advicebiblical #PowerOfChoice #Faith #Responsibility #GodsGuidance

works.title: "Why do I always have so many questions when I am alone?
works.description:
The text discusses the nature of human thought processes and how our brains handle multiple concerns simultaneously. It addresses the tendency for questions to arise when we lack immediate answers, and why we can’t always focus on specific thoughts at will. The author explains that our brains are designed to work on problems in the background while addressing more immediate matters in the foreground. This natural cognitive process allows individuals to manage different concerns effectively, emphasizing that it’s a blessing that our brains can multitask and work on problems even when they are not at the forefront of our attention.

#thinking #askquestions #biblical #advice #BrainPower #MultitaskingMind

works.title: "I don't want to be a bad parent, so I buy my kids whatever they want."
works.description:
The text discusses the misconception that being a good parent means giving children everything they want to shield them from hardship. The author argues that this approach prevents kids from learning to adapt to the real world, where not everything comes easily. Instead, they suggest that being a good parent involves teaching children about morality and modeling good behavior, regardless of material wealth. The author emphasizes that instilling a sense of morality and contentment, through teaching about God, will better equip children to navigate the world and make decisions. They caution against simply fulfilling children’s every desire, as it may hinder their ability to function effectively in society.

#biblicaltruth #biblicaladvice #wisewords #godlyfinances  #godlyparenting #Parenting #Morality #RealValues

works.title: "My past does not define me, I do"
works.description:
The text discusses the idea that while individuals may have the power to shape their future, it is also important to acknowledge the role of God in determining outcomes. The speaker suggests that solely relying on oneself to define the future can be dangerous and emphasizes the unpredictability of life. While advocating for personal empowerment, the speaker also urges caution against placing too much emphasis on individual control, highlighting the role of faith and the unknown in shaping one’s destiny.

#past #future #biblical #advice #Empowerment #Faith #Balance #Destiny

works.title: "I can't be a good spouse, because my partner is not listening to me"
works.description:
The text discusses the idea that being a good spouse is not solely dependent on whether your partner listens to you. Instead, it emphasizes personal responsibility and the commitment to being the best version of oneself in a relationship. The author suggests that despite challenges and difficulties, one should focus on their own actions and behaviors rather than using their partner’s actions as an excuse. The text acknowledges that maintaining a healthy relationship may be tough, but asserts that it’s essential to prioritize personal accountability and constructive efforts for the relationship to improve.

#biblical #advice #partner #RelationshipGoals #PersonalAccountability #SelfImprovement

works.title: "I am capable of setting my own limits and priorities"
works.description:
The text discusses the idea of setting personal limits and priorities within the context of free will and God’s boundaries. It emphasizes that while individuals have agency and can establish their own limits and priorities, these must align with the boundaries set by a higher power. The text suggests that going beyond these limits is not only unwise but also irrational, using the term “crazy” to describe such actions. Ultimately, it suggests that personal freedom exists within the framework of divine guidelines, and straying beyond these limits may lead to negative consequences.

#nolimits #priorities #Godsstory #bird #biblical #advice #church #EmbraceTheDivineBoundaries #HarmonyWithinLimits

works.title: "I am human, I make mistakes."
works.description:
The text discusses the phrase “I am human and I make mistakes” and delves into the speaker’s interpretation of this statement. The speaker finds it redundant, believing that everyone already knows humans make mistakes. They argue that saying this is an attempt to deflect from the truth, which is that the person wants to justify their mistakes. The speaker sees this as a weak excuse, suggesting that individuals should aim to be more than just human, particularly in the context of Christianity, striving to embody a redeemed and transformed self rather than simply accepting fallibility as a defining trait.

#human #mistakes #advice #biblical #Transformation #PurposefulLiving #SelfImprovement

works.title: "I can't satisfy all my needs but I am responsible to see them satisfied"
works.description:
The text discusses the concept of responsibility in meeting one’s needs. The speaker argues that while it is important to be a good steward of what one has, ultimately it is not solely one’s responsibility to ensure that their needs are met. Instead, the speaker suggests that it is God who is responsible for satisfying one’s needs, and trying to take on this responsibility oneself would detract from God’s role in the process. The speaker emphasizes the importance of working in concert with God rather than solely relying on personal effort to fulfill one’s needs.

#needs #godhelps #responsibility #biblicaladvice #FaithAndResponsibility #CollaborationWithGod #FindingBalance

works.title: "How I think or how I feel is not what I am"
works.description:
The text discusses the idea that a person’s thoughts and feelings do not fully define who they are. The speaker suggests that while thoughts and feelings are important, they are only part of a holistic being. They argue that as Christians, one is called to love God with all aspects of their being—heart, mind, and body—indicating that these elements work together. The speaker emphasizes that it’s problematic to compartmentalize different aspects of oneself, as identity should not be defined by separate compartments but rather by how God defines us. Ultimately, the text highlights the interconnectedness of different aspects of a person, forming a unified identity.

#feel #think #iam #biblicaltruth #life #Wholeness #FaithJourney #IdentityInGod

works.title: "It's okay to change my mind"
works.description:
The text discusses the concept of changing one’s mind, emphasizing that it’s important and acceptable to do so. The author highlights the need for flexibility in decision-making but cautions against using this as an excuse to detach from fundamental truths or values. While acknowledging the legitimacy of changing one’s mind, the text also underscores the necessity of remaining anchored to essential principles, such as those found in scripture, rather than using it as a means to justify negative behaviors.

#changemymind #biblicaltruth #advice #EmbraceChange #StayGrounded #WisdomInDecisionMaking

works.title: "What I want for myself is more important then what others want for me"
works.description:
The text explores the idea that prioritizing one’s own desires over the expectations of others is not wise. It argues that while it’s important not to be controlled by others, it’s also misguided to place excessive importance on one’s personal desires. Instead, the focus should be on understanding and aligning with what is best for the community and what God wants for an individual. The text suggests that those who prioritize their own desires over God’s will may face challenges and references biblical examples of people who suffered for prioritizing their own stories over God’s plan. Ultimately, the message emphasizes the importance of seeking and aligning with God’s will rather than placing undue importance on personal desires.

#biblicalcounseling #whatisimportant #putgodfirst #DivineWill #CommunityFirst #PurposefulLiving

works.title: "My feelings are just feelings neither good or bad"
works.description:
The text discusses the nature of feelings, arguing that not all feelings are neutral and that some are inherently bad. The speaker suggests that morality comes from a divine source and that certain feelings, such as the desire to kill or rape, are inherently bad and contrary to what a higher moral authority would want. The speaker emphasizes that not all feelings should be affirmed and that understanding the difference between good and bad feelings is crucial, rather than using the idea that all feelings are equal as an excuse for immoral behavior.

#biblicaltruth  #advice #goodfeeling #badfeelings #Emotions #Morality #UnderstandingFeelings #DeepThoughts

works.title: "I am responsible for my own happiness"
works.description:
The text discusses the idea of personal responsibility for happiness and raises questions about its validity. The author challenges the notion that individuals are solely responsible for their own happiness, suggesting that it may be an excuse to avoid involving others in their lives and to resist allowing others to have influence. The author proposes that this mindset might stem from a fear of connecting with people. Additionally, they argue that while individuals have agency in their lives, they do not possess all the power, cautioning against the belief that one has complete control. Furthermore, the author suggests that focusing solely on happiness may not be the right pursuit, emphasizing the importance of contentment and being okay with what one has. Ultimately, the text warns that those who believe they are solely responsible for their own happiness may encounter challenges, as this is a burden too significant for one person and may not be the most meaningful pursuit.

#biblicalwisdom #happinessadvice #biblicaladvice #FoodForThought #HappinessJourney #MeaningfulConnections

works.title: "I get to say it, because it important to me"
works.description:
The text emphasizes the importance of controlling what we say and the potential consequences of speaking without consideration. It highlights the idea that expressing one’s feelings should not be the sole basis for communication, as our emotions may not always guide us in the right direction. Instead, it advocates for thoughtful speech and the ability to listen before speaking. The text ultimately suggests that basing communication solely on feelings can lead to destructive outcomes.

#biblicaltruth #biblicaladvice #wisewords #speakwisely #bequiet #ThoughtfulSpeech #EffectiveCommunication #ListenBeforeSpeaking
